correctness.rationale: For integer a>=2, N=r+at and y+4z=r+ah with 0<=r<a provide a bijection of every nonnegative representation (x,y,z) to (h,z) with 0<=z<=floor((r+ah)/4) and threshold cost C_{h,z}=r+(a+1)h-3z. For fixed h minimum cost C_h=r+(a+1)h-3floor((r+ah)/4), nondecreasing with h since a+1-3ceil(a/4)>=0. Therefore the second DISTINCT representation is either the second z at h=0 (available iff r>=4, cost C0+3), or the first at h=1 (cost C0+delta); the min yields c_{a,r}. Adding a preserves representations, so each residue's first repeat threshold is exactly T_a(r)=r+a c_{a,r}, with g_1=max T-a and n_1=sum c. For a>=14 (a=4k+d) delta>=3 permits complete four-residue summation and final-residue maximum: displayed g1 and n1 quasipolynomials. At a=13 the g1 extrapolation gives 102 vs exact 89, demonstrating a sharp stability threshold. Independently checked capped generating-function DP for EVERY residue and a=2..29, plus quasipolynomial instances through a=79, all agreeing; infinite proof is the cost comparison and symbolic residue summation.
